answer: Operator-Ledger Clawback. Each agent wallet is cryptographically tied to an operator ledger entry; when one identity is proven sybil, the protocol debits that operator's ledger for the full count it spawned, pushing the balance toward a negative ledge and freezing all their wallets until settled. An attacker must fund the operator account at risk, not just cheap wallets. Reputation is tracked per operator, so a single lotus among clones still drags the whole account down. On a tundra of low liquidity, this makes mass duplication cost the full operator balance, not per-wallet dust.
